Convert a co-occurrence network to a cograph network

Source: R/converters.R
as_cograph.Rd

as_cograph() converts a co-occurrence network to a cograph_network. cograph draws and analyzes networks from a weight matrix, with layouts and styling designed for publication figures and functions for centrality and community detection. Its cograph_network class is also the base class of the networks estimated by Nestimate.

The cograph_network is built from the weight matrix returned by as_matrix(): a node table with one row per item and an edge table with one row per non-zero cell, one triangle for an undirected network and every off-diagonal cell for the directed similarity = "relative" network. The result can be passed to cograph::splot().

cograph exports its own as_cograph(). When cograph is attached after cooccure, a bare as_cograph() call resolves to the cograph version, which reads the edge data frame with its own defaults. Call cooccure::as_cograph(), or build the network with cooccurrence(..., output = "cograph"). For a result built with split_by, group names the network to convert.

Usage

as_cograph(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cooccurrence'
as_cograph(x, group = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A cooccurrence edge list from cooccurrence().

...

Ignored.

group

For a result built with split_by, the name of the group to convert. NULL (default) for an unsplit result.

Value

A list of class cograph_network holding the weight matrix (weights), a node table (one row per item: id, label, name, x, y), an edge table (one row per edge: integer from and to node ids and weight), directed (TRUE only for similarity = "relative"), and the node and edge counts.

Conditions

cooccure_missing_package when cograph is not installed; the conditions of as_matrix() for group.

See also

as_netobject() for the Nestimate class; as_igraph(); as_matrix().

Examples

net <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                    similarity = "jaccard", min_occur = 50)
if (requireNamespace("cograph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cooccure::as_cograph(net)
}
#> Cograph network: 12 nodes, 57 edges ( undirected )
#> Source: cooccure 
#>   Nodes (12): Action, Adventure, Animation, Biography, Comedy, Crime, ... +6 more
#>   Edges: 57 / 66 (density: 86.4%)
#>   Weights: [0.004, 0.285]  |  mean: 0.067
#>   Strongest edges:
#>     Adventure -- Animation  0.285
#>     Action -- Crime  0.237
#>     Comedy -- Drama  0.211
#>     Action -- Adventure  0.208
#>     Biography -- Documentary  0.204
#> Layout: none 
#>   Use as.data.frame() for the edge table, as.data.frame(what = "nodes") for the nodes.
